title: Longest Mountain in Array
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers `a[0] .. a[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the length of the longest mountain, or `0` if there is none.

examples.explanation: The subarray `1 3 5 4 2` rises to the peak 5 and then falls, giving length 5. The repeated `2 2` stops the descent, and `2 6 1` is only a mountain of length 3.
Every slope is flat, so there is no strictly increasing part and no mountain.
The mountain `1 4 7 3 2` has length 5. The trailing `2 5` rises again and cannot extend it.

hints: Every mountain has exactly one peak: an index that is strictly larger than both neighbours. How far can you extend left and right from such a peak?
For each peak, walk left while values strictly decrease and walk right while values strictly decrease. Total work stays linear because slopes of different peaks do not overlap.
Alternatively keep two counters in one scan: the length of the current climb and of the current descent. Reset them when a climb starts after a descent, or when two neighbours are equal.
